newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West electricity prices mostly steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West electricity prices mostly steady.

text.p: Wholesale spot electricity prices for the U.S. Mid-West were mostly steady Thursday despite a continued natural gas price hike, as traders looked for several generation units to return to service over the weekend, sources said.
IES Utilities Inc's 538 megawatt Duane Arnold nuclear power plant in Palo, Iowa was likely to reach full output over the weekend after a scheduled refueling and maintenance outage.
The 440 megawatt Big Stone coal-fired power plant in Big Stone City, S.D., will likely return to full service on Sunday after scheduled maintenance, Northwestern Public Service said.
MidAmerican Energy Co's 515 megawatt Neal coal fired power unit 3 near Sioux City, Iowa, was likely to resume production Thursday after being taken off line for a boiler tube leak.
Minnkota Power Cooperative said the 439 megawatt Milton Young coal-fired power unit 2 in Center, N.D., was likely to return to service Friday following boiler repairs.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm next day power deals were pegged steady to higher at $27.00-29.00 from $26.00-29.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Wednesday, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power prices were said to have eased to $14.00-16.00 from the $15.00-17.00 range on Wednesday.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) peak, non-firm power for Friday delivery was pegged steady at $23.00-25.00 from $22.00-26.00 on Wednesday.
Also, MAIN next day peak power in the north of the region was said to have been talked steady near $29.00 per MWh.
MAIN off peak power was assessed steady at $12.00-14.00.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Friday delivery were assessed lower at $20.00-21.50 from $25.00-28.00 on Wednesday.
Also, sources said ECAR next day peak power was being talked at $25.00-29.00 per MWh in the north area of the region.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was notionally assessed steady at $15.00-17.00 per MWh.
December peak ECAR was talked higher at $22.00-23.00 from $21.75-22.75 on Wednesday, the brokers and marketers said.
January/February ECAR was pegged higher at $23.00-24.00 from $23.00-23.30 per MWh.
Peak non-firm power prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) for Friday were talked steady to higher at $25.00-26.00 from $24.00-26.00 in Wednesday discussion, the sources said.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were notionally said to be steady in the $13.00-15.00 area, traders said.
December SPP was assessed lower at $26.50-27.50 from $27.75-28.75 on Wednesday, the brokers and marketers said.
